title: What contributing sends: your fix spans leave signed, the network proves them, and proven pairs join the public corpus
intro: Press play to walk the flow one step at a time, or click a dot to jump.

walk.title: Your fix run
walk.text: `cargo refine fix` runs on your machine and keeps only fixes that still compile. The once-per-install consent question runs first — the demo on the front page captures it verbatim. Each fix is recorded locally under `.refine/`. Logged out, this is where the story ends: nothing is uploaded.

walk.title: One row per fix
walk.text: A contribution row is the exact code span a fix replaced and its replacement, plus the rule name, a short numeric shape fingerprint and counters. File paths, crate names, repo URLs, git remotes and usernames are not fields. A span is your code verbatim, and one field may be up to 64 KiB — a long function a fix rewrote travels whole.

walk.title: Secret scan + sign
walk.text: Every span runs through the secret scanner — the consolidated provider-format set: API keys and tokens across the major AI, cloud and SaaS providers, private-key blocks (incl. PGP and PuTTY headers), credentialed connection strings, bearer tokens, secret assignments, long hex/base64 runs, and structured shapes like JWTs and bot tokens. Under the default policy any finding drops the whole row — it is never sent. The batch is signed with your account key, so the network can prove it is yours and untampered. The same scanner powers `cargo refine scan` and `scan --blind` on your side.

walk.title: Inspect first
walk.text: Nothing is sent before the consent answer, and the consent prompt (reproduced in the demo above) names exactly what sharing means. `cargo refine scan --blind FILE` shows what the scanner would redact in your own files before anything is ever shared. The published sample below is the batch shape the network's nodes push — read it before you join.

in.label: one batch (published sample)

walk.title: Sent over HTTPS
walk.text: A joined, consenting `cargo refine fix` sends the signed batch over HTTPS. The signature proves who sent it; it does not hide the content — the network must read a row to verify it.

walk.title: Proof queue
walk.text: Rows wait in the proof queue until a real clippy re-run confirms the fix. A verdict is measured, never trusted from the client. Unproven rows stay with the operator.

walk.title: Public corpus
walk.text: A proven row's before/after pair is published verbatim into the corpus segment — a public URL anyone can download without logging in. This is the shared corpus the flywheel promises; it is also why confidential code should stay out of your contributions.

walk.title: Lease back
walk.text: Every machine's corpus pull downloads the segment. The request carries only the version your machine already has — no code, no account — and your next run retrieves from what the fleet proved.
